issues.legal_issue: An occupant whose possession began with a tenant’s permission did not acquire adverse title against the landlord without a fresh assertion of hostile possession after the earlier adjudication, where the tenant continued paying rent and permitted the occupant to remain.
material_facts: The landlord had leased the house to the occupant’s brother, who allowed the occupant to live there.
The occupant asserted hostile title in a rent suit, but the tenant continued paying rent and allowed the occupant to stay in the house.
After the earlier adjudication, no fresh assertion of hostile possession by either the occupant or the tenant was proved.
The landlord obtained an eviction decree against the tenant, and the occupant sought a declaration of ownership by adverse possession and an injunction against eviction under that decree.
issues.conclusion: The occupant had not established adverse title against the landlord. The appeal was allowed, and the High Court’s judgments and decrees were set aside while the Senior Sub Judge’s decree was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Possession held with a tenant’s permission is not, without a sufficiently established hostile assertion, adverse to the landlord. In this case a fresh assertion of hostility after the earlier adjudication was required, and none was proved; the tenant’s rent payments and permission for the occupant to remain supported the finding that the occupation was not adverse. The judgment recounts the lower courts’ reference to Section 111(g) of the Transfer of Property Act, under which a landlord could determine a lease for denial of title, and to Kishwar Nath Sahi Dev v. Kali Shankar Sahai (1906) 10 Cal WN 343; the Supreme Court’s decision rests on the facts concerning the tenant’s continuing payments, the occupant’s permitted stay, and the absence of a fresh hostile assertion.

rule.if: adverse_possession_suit_against_landlord and occupant_entered_with_tenant_permission and tenant_continued_paying_rent and tenant_permitted_occupant_to_remain and no_fresh_hostile_assertion_after_earlier_adjudication

predicates.adverse_possession_suit_against_landlord: The proceeding sought to establish ownership by adverse possession against a landlord.
predicates.occupant_entered_with_tenant_permission: The occupant’s possession of the property began with permission from the landlord’s tenant.
predicates.tenant_continued_paying_rent: The tenant continued to pay rent to the landlord for the property.
predicates.tenant_permitted_occupant_to_remain: The tenant allowed the occupant to continue living in the property.
predicates.no_fresh_hostile_assertion_after_earlier: After an earlier adjudication, neither the occupant nor the tenant made a further proved assertion of hostile possession against the landlord.

issues.definition: When a person seeks adverse title against a landlord after entering through the landlord’s tenant, and the tenant continues paying rent and permits the person to remain without a fresh hostile assertion after an earlier adjudication, the person does not establish adverse title.
